title: Senior Receptionist
description: Working pattern: Full-time. Part-time would be considered. Job Location : Dorking Hospital, with travel and work across other DHC Outpatient sites. As a Senior Receptionist, you will play a key role in supporting the smooth running of reception services across DHC Outpatient locations. Working closely with the Lead Receptionist, you will help coordinate the day-to-day work of the reception team, support staff, assist with rota planning and act as a point of escalation for more complex patient enquiries or issues. The role combines hands-on reception duties with team support and operational coordination, helping to ensure patients, clinicians, and colleagues receive a professional, efficient, and compassionate service. We are looking for someone who is organised, proactive, reliable, and patient-focused. You will need excellent communication skills, strong administrative ability and the confidence to manage competing priorities in a busy outpatient environment. The successful candidate will be someone who takes ownership of tasks, works well under pressure, supports colleagues, maintains confidentiality, and is committed to improving the experience of patients and the wider team. We screen and shortlist suitable candidates as applications are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and without notice if we fill the position. Therefore, we encourage early applications to avoid disappointment. This is an excellent opportunity to join DHC Outpatients as part of an independent NHS organisation that values high standards, teamwork, and continuous improvement. You will be joining a service where your contribution can make a real difference to patients and colleagues every day, helping clinics run effectively, supporting the reception team, and playing an important part in delivering responsive, patient-centred outpatient care. As Senior Receptionist, you will help coordinate reception services across DHC Outpatient locations, ensuring patients receive a professional, efficient and welcoming service. Working with the Lead Receptionist, you will support team supervision, rota planning, training, service standards and escalation of complex patient enquiries. You will also help investigate incidents, monitor performance and fill vacant clinic appointments to maximise capacity and reduce waiting times. This role combines reception duties with leadership and operational support. We are looking for an organised, proactive and patient-focused individual with good communication, administration and IT skills. You will be confident in a busy environment, able to manage competing priorities, support colleagues, solve problems and maintain confidentiality. Attention to detail, a positive attitude, and a commitment to continuous improvement are essential. Training will be provided for our in-house IT systems; however good working knowledge of Microsoft Office is beneficial. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and the successful candidate must have an existing right to work in the UK. JOB SUMMARY The Senior Receptionist is responsible for supporting the Lead Receptionist in the day-to-day management and coordination of reception services across all DHC outpatient locations. Acting as deputy to the Lead Receptionist, the post holder will provide operational leadership to the reception team, ensuring high standards of patient service, administrative efficiency, and compliance with departmental procedures. The role combines hands-on reception duties with supervisory responsibilities, including staff support, rota coordination, training, performance monitoring, and ensuring reception functions are delivered effectively and consistently. The Senior Receptionist will act as the first point of escalation for more complex patient enquiries and service issues, exercising initiative, judgement, confidentiality, and diplomacy when resolving concerns. In the absence of the Lead Receptionist, the Senior Receptionist will oversee reception operations, allocate workloads, monitor performance indicators, and ensure appropriate staffing levels are maintained to support the smooth and effective delivery of outpatient services. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POST Support the Lead Receptionist in the day-to-day supervision and coordination of the reception team. Act as deputy for the Lead Receptionist during periods of absence, annual leave, or when off-site. Allocate daily responsibilities and monitor workload distribution to ensure efficient service delivery. Provide guidance, support, and coaching to reception staff to promote high performance and development. Assist with recruitment, induction, training, and competency assessments for new and existing team members. Support the completion of probation reviews, one-to-one meetings, appraisals, and development plans. Monitor staff attendance, punctuality, and compliance with departmental procedures, escalating concerns where appropriate. Assist in identifying training needs and opportunities for professional development. Produce and maintain team rotas, ensuring adequate staffing levels and reception cover across all DHC locations. Investigate incidents and record findings on the incident reporting platform. Coordinate adjustments to rotas to accommodate annual leave, sickness absence, training, and service requirements. Monitor reception performance against departmental KPIs and support improvement initiatives where required. Support the Lead Receptionist in reviewing patient feedback, complaints, and service performance metrics. Proactively contact patients to fill vacant clinic appointments, utilising waiting lists and cancellation lists to maximise clinic capacity and minimise unused appointment slots. Ensure reception processes comply with organisational policies, information governance requirements, and local procedures. Where required, act as a receptionist, which consists of: Being first point of contact for clinicians, staff, patients, carers, and service providers. Management of appointment bookings, cancellations, and rescheduling. Handling escalated patient concerns and complex enquiries. Maintaining accurate patient records. Answering incoming calls and responding to requests for information. Processing departmental mail. Attending relevant meetings and training sessions. Undertaking any other duties appropriate to the grade and nature of the role. WORK SETTING AND REVIEW To manage own workload efficiently and effectively on a daily basis. Maintain confidentiality at all times. Make decisions pertaining to the smooth and efficient running of DHC Operations, where necessary referring problems to senior management via the quickest route possible. Be able to work with a degree of autonomy . Work with a continuous improvement mindset. Work to objectives as set by the DHC Board of Directors. CONFIDENTIALITY The post holder must maintain the confidentiality of information about patients, staff and DHC business in accordance with the Data Protection Act 1998 and Caldicott principles.

title: Referrals Out Administrator
description: Referrals Out Administrators are an integral part of the Outpatients team, processing the onward referrals for patients who have been referred elsewhere for diagnostics or procedures. The key responsibilities are ensuring that referrals are sent within the expected timeframes, with all required information included, and actively monitoring the flow of information throughout the patient pathway. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and the successful candidate must have existing right to work in the UK. We screen and shortlist suitable candidates as applications are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and without notice if we fill the position. Therefore, we encourage early applications to avoid disappointment. Organisation, prioritisation, IT skills, and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be responsible for sending urgent and routine referrals to other providers and ensuring they have all the information needed to continue the patient's care. You will need to gather all the relevant information from different areas of the patient record system, including booking forms, clinic letters, BMI and blood results, and chase up any missing information with the clinicians or patients. Full training will be given on how to use our patient record system and complete the role. JOB SUMMARY The role (and team) is an integral part of the patient pathway. You will undertake tasks essential to the smooth and effective provision of quality care, providing an efficient level of service for patients and their families. The role will work within the priorities and expectations set out by the Lead Referrals-Out Administrator. It is essential the post holder displays organisation, prioritisation, IT skills and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be creating referrals on patient records to other providers. You will need to gather all the relevant information from the patient record system, submit it via email to the provider & update the patient record. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POST Referral Processing Process outbound referrals for diagnostics and procedures in line with clinical instructions and referral pathways. Ensure all referrals are correctly triaged, recorded, and actioned within agreed timeframes. Liaise with clinical teams and patients to clarify referral details or gather additional information as needed. Upload or send referrals via appropriate systems (e-RS, email, secure portals). Coordination & Communication Communicate clearly and professionally with external providers (e.g., hospitals, imaging centres, specialist clinics) to confirm referral receipt and appointment arrangements. Respond to incoming queries from patients, clinicians, and third parties regarding referrals, providing updates or advice as appropriate. Monitor referral progress and follow up to ensure timely outcomes or to troubleshoot delays. Managing multiple tasks, prioritising own workload, and ensuring work is completed within target timeframes for processing routine and urgent referrals. Work closely with the wider DHC administration and clinical teams to support seamless patient journeys. Pathway Knowledge & Relationship Management Ensure knowledge and understanding of patient pathways is maintained, including referral routes and any associated criteria for trust hospitals and independent providers. Develop and maintain relationships with other providers we work closely with. Sourcing new referral pathways, ensuring referral forms are updated, and the contact address database is maintained accurately. Contribute to maintaining and updating referral protocols and standard operating procedures. Data Management & Reporting Accurately input and update referral information in clinical systems to support timely patient care. Keep thorough documentation and audit trails in line with data protection and confidentiality policies. Contribute to performance monitoring through accurate data capture and referral tracking insights. General Undertake any other reasonable duties as commensurate with the nature of this role. Acting independently but, where necessary, referring problems to the Referrals-Out Team Leader or the appropriate consultant via the quickest route possible.
